newsitem.title: USA: Florida tobacco trial suspended until Monday.
newsitem.headline: Florida tobacco trial suspended until Monday.

text.p: The judge in a wrongful-death trial against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. ordered Friday that testimony of a key plaintiff witness resume on Monday after a juror fell ill.

Circuit Court Judge Bernard Knachman sent the jury home early for weekend after the sick juror failed to report back on his ailment. Knachman said he would put off until Monday a decision on whether or not to replace the ill juror.

When court was suspended, Dr. Allan Feingold, a pulmonary specialist, was testifying on behalf of the family of Jean Connor, a 49-year-old woman and long-time smoker who died of lung cancer two years ago.
R.J. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
